findings.text: follow-on: The node's own FENCE-EVIDENCE names the evidence fragment as a deliverable: 'the evidence fragment states which guarantee the fix gives and whether the live index takes it only after the ingest service restarts, citing logs under the node's report directory'. That fragment was granted in the node's write paths and is not present at the reviewed head (test -f returns false; the fragment set under docs/evidence/fragments/serving-record-warehouse/ lists no srw-ledger-carriers-never-split-runs.html), and the commit changes only imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py, tests/test_ledger_additive_identity.py and tests/test_ingest_carrier_overlap.py. Reproduced: `git show --stat 0957a37e` lists exactly those three files, +365/-7. The content the fragment owed -- which guarantee the fix gives, and that the live index takes it only once the ingest and publisher services are restarted -- is stated in the manifest 'landing:' line, but the durable, reviewable, per-node artifact the plan's fragment set expects is missing. This is one of the four clauses of the node's done-when; the other three are met.

follow_ons.text: The missing fragment (see findings) should be authored from the manifest landing line and the node's own logs before this run's evidence set is read as complete; a later node or the coordinator owns it.

The fix corrects the run-boundary predicate (counter_run_continues -> _same_run), which both the query path (partitioned_total -> _counter_runs) and the compactor share, so no index state can inflate a total once the running services load the new code. The live index therefore takes the fix only once the ingest and publisher services are restarted, which is out of this node's scope and correctly recorded in the reviewed manifest.

item_verdicts.implementation: counter_run_continues now calls _same_run(previous[0], current[0]); _same_run requires host and job equal and treats an empty boot marker as compatible with any boot, ending the run only when two keys both declare a boot and disagree. This is the mechanism 13 located: the raw file's null boot and the tier's real boot no longer split the run at every alternation, so a tier row no longer re-adds its stride through its declared opening.

justifications: Independent review of run r-20261005T084405666372-srw-ledger-carriers-never-split-runs, reviewed_run_id, base 53e200991da706a0e9648c934ccb690ab76d8cdf, head 0957a37e2879e0228cbe21ed53bb115aecf379f5, stored as a parsed record scoring all five dimensions in 0..20 -- goal_fidelity 16, evidence 17, scope_discipline 19, durability 16, fit 17 -- total 85, added_failure_count 0 with added_failure_ids [] derived from this review's own two arms of the reviewed node's declared gate (the reviewed run was dispatched unarmed, so its own baseline_suite and after_suite are null): base arm logs/review-base-arm.log (scratch tree $TMPDIR/arms/base, revision 53e20099, head test files overlaid: 5 failed, EXIT=1) and head arm logs/review-head-arm.log (scratch tree $TMPDIR/arms/head, revision 0957a37e: 5 passed, EXIT=0). The fix is at the mechanism, not a clamp: counter_run_continues now defers the run boundary to _same_run, which holds host and job fixed and lets the empty boot marker (a raw row) continue the same run while two declared, differing boots end it; the same predicate serves partitioned_total's _counter_runs and the compactor. Both tests measure the additive identity the plan names -- a day equals the sum of its 24 hours for prompt tokens, generation tokens and each cached tier -- the first from fixture raw rows (null boot) beside minute-tier rows (real boot) read together, the second by driving the real ingest over hour, minute and raw files in small batches and reading the index after every commit. The negative control was reproduced independently rather than accepted: re-applying the defect on the head tree (restoring `previous[0] != current[0]` as the run test in a scratch copy) reddens all five cases (5 failed, EXIT=1, logs/review-negative-control.log), a stronger red than the reviewed run's own control (4 failed, 1 passed). ruff check imas_ambix tests exits 0 (logs/review-ruff.log) and the serving-interpreter parse guard passes, 2 passed 7 deselected (logs/review-parse-guard.log). One finding: the node's done-when names an evidence fragment stating which guarantee the fix gives and whether the live index takes it only after restart, and no such fragment exists at head -- the content lives only in the manifest landing line. That clause is unmet; the other three done-when clauses hold, and the fix itself is verified sound.
